newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil police expels nine video brutality officers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil police expels nine video brutality officers.

text.p: Sao Paulo's military police force on Wednesday expelled nine of the 11 men allegedly involved in a videotaped incident of police violence that shocked Brazil, Globo television said.

Amateur footage first aired three months ago showed police officers torturing and intimidating civilians at a roadblock in suburban Sao Paulo and one policeman firing a shot at a car, hitting a passenger who later died.
The video, shown repeatedly on several channels, triggered a wave of public outcry against police abuses and prompted the creation of a government human rights commission.
On Wednesday, a military police disciplinary committee ruled that two of the men identified in the video be sent to jail.

The other nine were expelled, including Officer Otavio Lourenco Gambra, nicknamed "Rambo" by the Brazilian media, who was accused of the videotaped killing. Gambra has admitted firing a shot near the car but said he was aiming at the floor.
A civilian court investigating accusations against 10 of the men expected to sentence the officers before the end of the year.
The disciplinary committee's decision came at a time when Brazil's military police has once again been cast under a harsh spotlight.
A police officer was shot in the head last week during a demonstration by colleagues striking for better wages in Minas Gerais. He later died of his injuries.
Officials said the violent protest, which ended with the police officers obtaining a 48 percent salary increase, could trigger a wave of copycat strikes across the country.
Studies show many officers live on low wages and some resort to crime to supplement their official income.
